recipes.name: Cauliflower Fritters
ingredients_raw: 1 (.7 ounce) package dry Italian-style salad dressing mix
0.5 cup olive oil for frying, or as needed

steps.text: Process cauliflower in a food processor finely minced; transfer to a large bowl.
Stir flour, eggs, baking powder, and Italian dressing mix into cauliflower.
Heat enough olive oil to cover the bottom of a frying pan over medium heat.
Drop heaping tablespoons of cauliflower mixture into the hot oil; fry until golden brown, about 3 minutes per side.

raw_recipe.headline: Cauliflower Fritters
raw_recipe.description: These cauliflower fritters are easy to prepare and a different way to eat cauliflower. They are a great appetizer to serve your family and friends.

video.description: See how easy it is to turn cauliflower into delicious fritters.

review.reviewBody: This is a "wow" on the tongue! I was pleasantly surprised. Read all reviews before starting, so I food processed yellow banana peppers and red onion in with the cauli. We only had one head of cauliflower, so I cut recipe in half. Next time I'll get another head of cauliflower! As we don't keep Italian dressing in the house I just added a mix of what might be equivalent: marjoram, sweet basil, kelp, freshly squeezed garlic, chives, parsley, tarragon, thyme, celery salt . . . but it still was lacking punch, so I added quite a bit of salt and then some paprika. Once it fried in the olive oil (with a wee bit of butter cut in), it was amazing! Thank you for this. I can see adding leftover mashed potatoes to the mix, kale, or artichoke hearts next time. It's a very flexible recipe--heat it up, mellow it out--all in your personal taste & preferences. Will stick this one in the recipe box to use again & again. And, no leftovers at all--phenomenal with a little aioli garlic mustard sauce on top, too! mmMMMmmm.

very good and easy. but i added grated romano cheese (parmesan works too) as per suggestions from others who left reviews. i put 1/4 cup but next time I'll use more-1/2 cup probably. to reheat-i used air fryer--Fabulous!! maybe better the next day reheated in air fryer--so make a double batch so you have lots of leftovers!!

Made a vegan version of this, as a side dish to my vegan chilli. Instead of using three eggs, I used flax eggs (1 tbsp powder flax seed + 3 tbsp water = 1 flax egg). I didn’t have Italian dressing mix. So, used used 1 tbsp Italian seasoning plus salt, black pepper, and smoked paprika to taste. I think I also processed my cauliflower florets too much. Next, time I’ll give it two fewer pulses. Turned out delicious though!

These are pretty amazing! However when We made them, they went onto the George Foreman Grill. Brushed the grill with a tiny bit of Peanut oil before putting the fritters on and cooked until well browned. Sprinkled with a bit of Kosher Salt as soon as they came out. They were gone in a flash.
I cooked these in my air fryer. 8 minutes on each side, 350 degrees. Excellent!

This recipe was super easy. I’ve got plenty of time being home because of the COVID-19 pandemic. It took 3 food processor fulls of cauliflower pulsing. I made my own dry Italian seasoning because I didn’t have any. I added 4 eggs because mine were only large, not x-large. I added a shake or two of cayenne because we like a bite of heat. I added a touch more flour and added a handful of Romano cheese. The batter stayed together while frying. These were the best fritters I’ve achieved in my fritter history. I made a garlic lemon aioli, which doesn’t dominate like a marinara sauce, and allowed the fritter flavor to meld nicely with the aioli.

This recipe was good, but I made some tweaks to add flavor. I sautéed up some garlic and a jalepeno pepper and added that to the batter. Next time I will add even more of those ingredients. I used Italian seasoning instead of the salad dressing. And for even cooking I flattened out the fritters, so they were more like cauliflower pancakes.

Love this concept! It is a good base for a great side dish. I don't know what a package of salad dressing would do since I didn't use one (I used about a tsp of basil and a tbls oregano instead). This way the flavor was good but a bit to plain for my taste. The second time I added about 1 tsp smoked paprika, 1/4 tsp powdered coriander, 2 tbls dry sage, a big pinch of powdered chipotle, s & p and it was far more interesting.

Overall was yummy and easy. Needed more seasoning to my taste. Would rather add my own seasonings than the powdered dressing. Sauted some onion and added to batter. Also to get it browned took more oil than i usually use. But soaked it up with paper towels. Nice with apple sause like latkes. Would make again got thumbs up from the family for a "super food".

Absolutely yummy! I made some changes in the cauliflower prep. I had baked a whole cauliflower from the night before and had lots of leftovers. I cut off the florets from the stalk. I mashed them with a potato masher which left some chunkiness to the mix. The rest I followed to the tee. Crunchy on the outside, soft on the inside. Next time I will try broccoli with cauliflower.

Since you can also eat the stalks of cauliflower I just ground up large chunks, florets, stalks and all in my food processor. Didn't use italian dressing but just seasoned with thyme, basil, kosher salt. Preparation is very easy, frying takes a bit of time.

I rarely leave ratings for recipes I find online, but I must tell you this is an excellent recipe. I added a bit of finally graded Parmesan to the mixture. That was the only change I made and they turned out fantastic. I fried them in olive oil on fairly high heat and they browned up with a really nice crust. I made a dipping sauce using mayonnaise, a bit of maple syrup and sriracha hot sauce. I used a recipe to make my own Italian blend and used it in the recipe as well as making a dressing for the side salad I served with the fritters. This will be a regular in our lunch rotation. Thank you so much for sharing the recipe.
loved it

Very delicious and you can top with anything (personal favorite was sriacha with vegetables piled ontop). I was looking for a cheap meal to pack in my lunch, so as a warning they do get soggy when cooled. I also cooked them without oil so they turned out a little less crispy, so I might try them in the airfryer and see how that works out. Very addicting, friends love it, honestly will make again.

I added some red pepper flakes and some green onions, but otherwise left the recipe as written. It’s very good. Everyone loved it! I found a recipe on this website for Italian dressing mix which has a lot of flavor, also a lot of salt. I believe the conversion for .7 ounces is 1.4 tablespoons. But you might want to doublecheck that.
yum, added parmi, and had no italian dressing pak, but will get for next time, found my italian seasonings, over all though -what a great way to eat a patty.
Followed recipe exactly. Added minced garlic too. Had to add a TON of salt and black pepper to add any flavor. Cooked them on the Blackstone. They were ok, probably won't be making them again
Super easy to make, easy to follow instructions and delicious.

I used a bag of organic riced cauliflower with 4 egg whites, added a little black pepper, pink Himalayan sea salt and some garlic powder which really made a difference to me. Also, I served these with a little spaghetti sauce to dip them in alongside some Tofurkey Italian Soy Sausages. Perfecto!
I just made it on a whim. so I had not Italian dressing mix. I made it for lunch tried it with different low calorie salad dressing. Not bad at all.
